import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 20.76
by L. Pyber
*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v40)
!-/
namespace Kourovka.«20.76»
/--
Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group and assume that all abelian normal subgroups of $G$
have order at most $p^k$. Is it true that every abelian subgroup of $G$ has order at most
$p^{2k}$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka_20_76 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ᵉ (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (hg : IsPGroup p G) (_ : Finite G) (k : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ H: Subgroup G, H.Normal ∧ IsMulCommutative H → Nat.card H ≤ p ^ k),
    (∀ H : Subgroup G, IsMulCommutative H → Nat.card H ≤ p ^ (2 * k)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«20.76»

reformulations.difference: Mathlib expresses the p-group condition elementwise, as ∀ g, ∃ n, g^(p^n) = 1, and expresses an abelian subgroup through commutativity of its subtype's inherited multiplication.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under p.Prime and Finite G, IsPGroup.iff_card identifies the elementwise condition with ∃ n, Nat.card G = p^n. IsMulCommutative H is equivalent to ∀ x ∈ H, ∀ y ∈ H, x*y = y*x in G. Every subgroup is finite, so Nat.card H is its ordinary order. The complete right-hand side was proved equivalent to an unpacked formulation using these characterizations and separately stated normality and commutativity hypotheses.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states Problem 20.76. Quantifier scope, the yes/no answer slot, normality, and both non-strict bounds agree with the source. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully without relying on the admitted conjecture. They establish the full unpacked equivalence, show that k = 0 forces G to be trivial, verify hypothesis satisfiability, and test trivial, cyclic-order-two, and dihedral-order-eight cases. The latest checked source, v46, remains consistent with research open. The target file was not modified.
